newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money rises on liquidity reports.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money rises on liquidity reports.

text.p: Jakarta call money rose to 15.0/15.5 percent from 12.5/13.5 percent on the back of rising rupiah demand on liquidity reporting, dealers said.
They said the last day for liquidity reports and weekly tax payments due Tuesday seemed to cause higher demand amid early central bank injection of 545 billion rupiah.
One foreign bank dealer said the last liquidity reporting day might have also caused operators to square positions they had opened following recent aggresive swap selling.
He said this might have driven short-dated swap rates to increase and thus driving short-term money to follow.
Overnight swaps rose to 0.55/0.65 from 0.15/0.25. Tom/next swap was last at 0.40/0.47 points.

However, the central bank still offered overnight bilateral SBIs at seven percent, 2-3 day at 7.5 percent, 6-8 percent at 9.5 percent, 9-10 at 10.5 percent, 13-14 at 11.25 percent, one-month at 12.0 percent, three at 13.0 percent, six- at 13.25 and 12-month at 13.50 percent.
Longer-term money was little changed, with one-month quoted at 12.75/12.875 percent and three-month at 13.75/14.00 percent.
The average overnight interbank money on Monday was 8.38 percent, compared with 8.48 percent on Friday.
